$comment: D-C-PREPROCESSED-INPUT-REFUSES-GCC-LINEMARKERS: the GNU LINEMARKER `# N "file" [flags]` — what `gcc -E` / `clang -E` write where a `#line` would go — is accepted and SETS the presumed position. At the pre-change HEAD every such TU died on `error[P0015] unsupported preprocessor directive: 1`, so a conformance census had to run `-E -P` and discard exactly the file/line provenance it wanted. FOUR arms, each scored 0 by a different plausible wrong implementation: (1) the presumed LINE is read from a marker carrying the full gcc flag tail `1 3 4`, so an implementation that parsed the number and choked on the flags mis-numbers; (2) it is read again under the OTHER nesting flag `2`, so enter/return are not two half-features; (3) the presumed FILE drives `__FILE__` and is read at two markers whose names differ in their FIRST byte, so an implementation that set the line but not the name scores 0 while passing 1 and 2; (4) line number ZERO is accepted, which C23 6.10.4p2 forbids for `#line` and which gcc's own `-E` output opens with (MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 emits `# 0 "tu.c"` and recompiles its own output rc=0). ANTI-FOLD: the score is multiplied by a runtime `argc` predicate so the release pipeline cannot reduce main to a constant return. Data-model-independent (int arithmetic and byte comparisons only), so the one exit code holds on all four targets and on the shipped release pipeline. exit = 10 + 10 + 12 + 10 = 42.
